eligibility:
Eligible branches: CSE, ECE, Electrical
Criteria: 7.5 and above CGPA with no active and Passive backlogs
selection_procedure: Initial CV/cg shortlisting for the online test, followed by online test, 2 technical and 1 HR round
test_description: The test consisted of Aptitude/ Quant, english MCQs followed by 2 DSA questions
test_preparation: For DSA, focus on standard LeetCode medium problems. For other sections, I didn't prepare explicitly but recommend Indiabix for English aptitude and quant, Codehelp (Luv Babbar) for mock tests, and GeeksforGeeks archives for additional practice.
interview_experience:
The interview process consisted of two technical rounds and one HR round.  

First Technical Round:
The first 10-15 minutes focused on my summer internship, as the interviewer was curious about my transition from the semiconductor field to tech. DSA questions followed, including variations of the "Valid Parentheses" problem (e.g., generating and finding the length of the longest valid parentheses). Then, I was asked 2-3 ML questions related to my deep learning project. This was followed by data and SQL questions based on my internship experience, as well as basic SQL concepts like views and joins.  

Second Technical Round:
It started with a brief discussion about my summer internship. I was then asked to write code to print a triangular wave, followed by questions on memory allocation, pointers, and OOP concepts in C++.  

HR Round:
This round primarily revolved around my summer internship, exploring why I wanted to transition to tech and how my TI experience could benefit Wells Fargo. Behavioral questions included managing teams, handling pressure, and maintaining work ethics within Wells Fargo’s culture. The discussion ended on an informal note about the interviewer’s experiences in Jaipur, including its food, people, and culture.
important_topics: DSA, one of the object oriented languages (C++/Java) very well in depth, and in depth understanding of everything  you have mentioned in your CV.
preparation_start: Starting of 2nd year.
junior_advice:
For 1st Year Students:
Explore everything and gain clarity on what you want to pursue. Start learning a programming language, get familiar with coding, and enjoy the process and college life. Maintain a CGPA above 8+ (it’s manageable and will benefit you in the long run). Remember, CGPA matters in almost every aspect of your career.  

For 2nd Year Students:
Start early—devote 1.5-2 hours daily to DSA, but balance it with other enjoyable activities. Consistency will likely help you land a summer internship by the beginning of your 3rd year.  

For 3rd Year Students: 
Focus on core CS fundamentals and projects while continuing with DSA. Don’t stress if you’re not clearing OA’s or interviews. Stay confident and consistent—success will follow.

Test preparation:
To prepare for such aptitude-based tests, one should regularly practice quantitative aptitude, logical reasoning, and verbal ability questions using standard aptitude books and online platforms. Websites like GeeksforGeeks (GFG) are especially helpful, as they provide structured practice questions, explanations, and mock tests. Practicing within a fixed time limit is important to improve both speed and accuracy. Strengthening basic mathematical concepts, improving reading comprehension, and solving puzzles can further enhance analytical skills. Preparing for these tests not only helps for Blue Matters, but also proves beneficial for almost all company recruitment exams.

Interview experience:
There were two rounds of interviews.

1. Case Interview Round:
Before the interview, we were given a case study containing around four analytical questions. We had about an hour to analyze the case, solve the questions, and prepare notes. During the interview, I discussed each question with the interviewer, presented my solutions, and received feedback. It was a very interactive and discussion-based round where we collaboratively arrived at the best possible approaches. Toward the end, the interviewer also asked about my hobbies and extracurricular positions of responsibility.

2. Personal Interview (HR) Round:
This round included around 4–5 high-level aptitude and guesstimate questions. I was also asked why I wanted to join Blue Matter, followed by discussions on my projects and internships. A few questions related to my technical skills were also asked in this round. Overall, the interview process was engaging, analytical, and conversational in nature.

The company expects candidates to have strong basic concepts and good problem-solving ability rather than just mugged-up knowledge.

Good command over aptitude, logical reasoning, and analytical thinking is important since many evaluations focus on how you think and approach problems.

For SDE roles, they look for understanding of data structures & algorithms, coding concepts, OOPs, DBMS, and OS basics.

For Data/Analytics roles, having clarity in statistics, probability, SQL, Excel, Python/R basics, and the ability to understand and interpret data really helps.

They value candidates who can break down problems logically, explain their thoughts clearly, and communicate confidently.

Being aware of industry trends, showing interest in learning, and having a growth mindset also creates a strong positive impression.

For most of the company's OA striver A2Z DSA sheet is enough but some companies do ask problems based on competitive programming

And after solving 100 problems you can start CP in parallel and try to solve problems of graphs since they do come in OA

The second round (Tech + HR) involved detailed project discussions, feature-building tasks, and some technical questions. Every point mentioned in resume

At last , be confident do not revise/ discuss study at the last moment before interview it creates panic...and try to communicate with the interviewer and ensure you both are on the same page

Additionally, I was asked questions related to OOPs concepts, REST APIs, authentication, machine learning, and big data basics.

Technical Interview – Round 2:
The second round was more project-oriented. I explained why I chose certain projects, how I built them, and the reasoning behind my tech stack. HR Interview:
The HR round was relaxed and conversational, covering basic behavioral questions and my understanding of the company.

1. Strong understanding of Data Structures and Algorithms with good problem-solving skills.
2. Ability to clearly explain projects, practical applications, and design decisions.
3. Strong understanding of machine learning and big data concepts is valued.

5. Comfort with basic backend concepts including APIs, authentication mechanisms, and system workflows.
